Oslo : Essential Oslo, City Center Guided Walking Tour | 10 AM | 2 Hrs | Experience the beauty of the Norwegian capital on foot with this walking tour See all the major sights and attractions in a pedestrian part of Oslo Save money with this great value pass Meet our guide near the University of Oslo, Start your day with a guided walking tour of Oslo's most popular sights and landmarks. *From 17 November to 30 December, the Christmas Walk will replace the Essential Oslo Tour. Explore the major attractions of the vibrant Norwegian capital on our bestselling city tour. Meet our guide near the University of Oslo, in the city’s heart, and embark on a thrilling urban adventure! First, you will visit the modern Oslo Opera House, which quickly became the city’s icon after its construction in 2008. Our guide will tell you about this building and the radical transformation of the neighborhood, which occurred during the last two decades. Next, you will stroll down Karl Johans gate, the city’s emblematic two-lane central street. That’s where you can truly appreciate Oslo's stunning 19th-century architecture. We will make the first stop on this street near Domkirke, or as the locals gently call this cathedral—the “Dom.” The city’s main church was built in the late 17th century and substantially reconstructed during the 19th century. Follow our guide’s lead and see the other prominent buildings on Oslo’s main street. Stortinget, the Parliament building, was erected during the second part of the 19th century when Norway was in a forced union with Sweden. You will also notice the Grand Hotel building nearby—renowned playwright Henrik Ibsen used to frequent its café. A statue dedicated to Ibsen stands in front of the neighboring National Theater, not far from another one that depicts Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson. The majestic Royal Palace of Oslo stands on a hill at the end of the street. Even though it was built for the very person this street is named after, Karl Johan has never got a chance to reside in this magnificent palace. Our tour guide will delve deeper into the story of the French general-turned-Swedish king and how he became the ruler of Norway. Before the tour concludes, you will visit one more iconic building—the red-brick Oslo City Hall. Its construction took decades to finish, but today, this place embodies the spirit of Oslo (and Norway in general)—the walls of this building are painted with numerous frescoes depicting the history of this Scandinavian country. Join our walking tour today to explore Oslo in a fun and exciting way!

Oslo : Essential Oslo, City Center Guided Walking Tour | 10 AM | 2 Hrs | Experience the beauty of the Norwegian capital on foot with this walking tour See all the major sights and attractions in a pedestrian part of Oslo Save money with this great value pass Meet our guide near the University of Oslo, Start your day with a guided walking tour of Oslo's most popular sights and landmarks. *From 17 November to 30 December, the Christmas Walk will replace the Essential Oslo Tour. Explore the major attractions of the vibrant Norwegian capital on our bestselling city tour. Meet our guide near the University of Oslo, in the city’s heart, and embark on a thrilling urban adventure! First, you will visit the modern Oslo Opera House, which quickly became the city’s icon after its construction in 2008. Our guide will tell you about this building and the radical transformation of the neighborhood, which occurred during the last two decades. Next, you will stroll down Karl Johans gate, the city’s emblematic two-lane central street. That’s where you can truly appreciate Oslo's stunning 19th-century architecture. We will make the first stop on this street near Domkirke, or as the locals gently call this cathedral—the “Dom.” The city’s main church was built in the late 17th century and substantially reconstructed during the 19th century. Follow our guide’s lead and see the other prominent buildings on Oslo’s main street. Stortinget, the Parliament building, was erected during the second part of the 19th century when Norway was in a forced union with Sweden. You will also notice the Grand Hotel building nearby—renowned playwright Henrik Ibsen used to frequent its café. A statue dedicated to Ibsen stands in front of the neighboring National Theater, not far from another one that depicts Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson. The majestic Royal Palace of Oslo stands on a hill at the end of the street. Even though it was built for the very person this street is named after, Karl Johan has never got a chance to reside in this magnificent palace. Our tour guide will delve deeper into the story of the French general-turned-Swedish king and how he became the ruler of Norway. Before the tour concludes, you will visit one more iconic building—the red-brick Oslo City Hall. Its construction took decades to finish, but today, this place embodies the spirit of Oslo (and Norway in general)—the walls of this building are painted with numerous frescoes depicting the history of this Scandinavian country. Join our walking tour today to explore Oslo in a fun and exciting way!

This safari is a van-based activity, and includes a traditional Swedish midsummer meal. What's included? Transport by private minivan English-speaking wildlife guide Free photo memories by the guide Traditional Swedish meal Pick up / meeting point : Stockholm Adventure, Kungsbro strand 21, Stockholm What to expect? In Stockholm, as is always the case in Sweden, nature is never far away. Just beyond the city limits are extensive lush forests and plenty of farming and agricultural land that are inhabited by a vast array of wildlife. Here, moose, deer, foxes, hares and wild boar roam undisturbed. Our Wildlife Safari runs during dusk, which is an optimal time to go in search of animals, and in particular, the “Kings of the Forest” (moose) who usually roam at sundown to graze and search for water. Your guide welcomes you on board our small and comfortable minivan before heading out of the city and into one of Stockholm’s most wildlife-rich areas. Once out in nature and before starting the safari proper, get to know your safari companions and enjoy a traditional Swedish midsummer meal at an outdoor camp. Your knowledgeable guide takes this time to explain more about the habitat surrounding you and the animals that inhabit it. You then navigate through rural landscapes characterised by traditional red cottages, classic manor houses, majestic forests and historical rune stones from the Viking age, searching for wildlife. We do so by van so as to cover a greater distance and increase your chances of spotting wildlife; we usually see at least three out of five of the animals mentioned, if not all five! Once the sun has set, you return to the city. We offer open/scheduled departures and private departures. Our traditional Swedish midsummer meal consists of three different herrings, freshly boiled potatoes, meatballs, sausages, boiled eggs with Kalles Kaviar and hard crispy bread with Västerbotten Cheese. Gothenburg: Private | Discover the City Boat Ride in Goth-River | 10:30 | 2 hrs Overview Private tour ◉ Pickup available ◉ Tour guide What's included? Hotel pick-up service Private transfer in AC vehicle Parking fees and WiFi English-speaking captain Sightseeing and guidance Bottled water and snacks What to expect? Set sail on a captivating boat ride along the Göta River, where history and scenery come together. Feel the breeze as you glide through Gothenburg’s hidden gems and iconic landmarks. With our expert guide, uncover 400 years of history, from the majestic King Gustav Adolf’s Statue to the charming German Church and the legendary Feskekörka (Fish Church). Gothenburg Boat Tour – Explore the City from the Water At your requested time, our professional tour guide will pick you up from your hotel in Gothenburg and drive you to the city center, where your boat tour begins. This experience offers a unique way to explore Gothenburg while feeling the fresh breeze on your face as you cruise through its scenic waterways. Lejontrappan – The Starting Point Your journey begins at Lejontrappan ("The Lion Stairs"), one of Gothenburg's most well-known landmarks. This historic staircase, located in the heart of the city, serves as a popular meeting point and the departure location for your boat ride. Gustav Adolfs Square & Historic Landmarks As you sail along the Göta River, you’ll pass Gustav Adolfs Square, where you’ll see the statue of King Gustav II Adolf, the founder of Gothenburg, which has stood in the square since the late 17th century. You will also admire the Stock Exchange Market Building and City Hall, both dating back to the 17th century and reflecting Neoclassical architecture. The German Church (Christinae Church) Your boat ride continues past The German Church, also known as Christinae Church, named after Queen Christina of Sweden. Inaugurated in 1748, this historic church once served the German and Dutch communities in Gothenburg and remains a significant landmark in the city center. Lilla Bommen – The Harbor & Iconic Sights Enjoy sailing into the North Sea as you reach Lilla Bommen, a key part of Gothenburg’s harbor. This area is home to the Göteborg Opera House, the Viking Barque Ship, and the distinctive Läppstiftet ("The Lipstick"), a red-and-white skyscraper offering panoramic city views. Water and snacks will be provided during the tour. Feskekörka – The Fish Church Cruising further along the Göta River, you will pass Feskekörka ("Fish Church"), a unique indoor fish market designed in Neo-Gothic style. Opened in 1874, this landmark, designed by architect Victor von Gegerfelt, is an essential stop for seafood lovers and architectural enthusiasts alike. Final Landmarks & Return As the tour continues, you will pass Stora Teatern, a historic theater known for its striking architecture, and Trädgårdsföreningen, a beautiful 19th-century garden park. At the end of the boat tour, we will drive you back to your hotel, concluding your memorable journey through Gothenburg’s waterways

Copenhagen: Forest Tower & Forgotten Giants Day Tour | 10 AM | 5.5 Hrs Pick up / meeting point : Colbjørnsensgade 15, Copenhagen Overview TIME Magazine named the Forest Tower one of the 100 greatest places to visit worldwide in 2019. Enjoy a visit to this architectural masterpiece, set in the heart of one of the country’s most scenic forest landscapes. What's included? Pick-up/drop-off from central Copenhagen Transportation by air-conditioned minibus Guided visit to Copenhagen Forest Tower Guided visit to The Forgotten Giants site Not Included Entrance ticket to Forest Tower Food and drinks are excluded What to expect? Visitors follow a 1.2‑kilometer elevated wooden boardwalk that winds gently through the treetops. The path leads to the Forest Tower itself, a striking 45‑meter spiraling structure rising above the canopy. Walking the tower’s curved ramp offers a calm, panoramic ascent where the forest opens up step by step. At the top, the 360‑degree view stretches across rolling woodlands, lakes, and fields, making it one of the most photogenic spots in Denmark. Many travelers describe standing on the summit of this “wooden skyscraper” as a highlight of their entire trip. The Forgotten Giants: A Modern Fairy Tale Hidden in Nature The “Forgotten Giants” are a beloved outdoor art treasure scattered around the outskirts of Copenhagen. Created by Danish artist Thomas Dambo, the project features six enormous wooden sculptures built entirely from recycled materials and locally sourced scrap wood. Each giant is placed in a quiet, natural setting - meadows, forests, lakesides - encouraging visitors to explore lesser‑known green areas around the city. Every sculpture has its own personality and story, and part of the charm is the sense of discovery. They are intentionally hidden, turning the visit into a playful treasure hunt for adults and children alike. On this tour, we visit two of these impressive giants, giving you time to walk around them, appreciate the craftsmanship, and enjoy the peaceful surroundings where they rest.

Gustav Adolfs Square & Historic Landmarks As you sail along the Göta River, you’ll pass Gustav Adolfs Square, where you’ll see the statue of King Gustav II Adolf, the founder of Gothenburg, which has stood in the square since the late 17th century. You will also admire the Stock Exchange Market Building and City Hall, both dating back to the 17th century and reflecting Neoclassical architecture. The German Church (Christinae Church) Your boat ride continues past The German Church, also known as Christinae Church, named after Queen Christina of Sweden. Inaugurated in 1748, this historic church once served the German and Dutch communities in Gothenburg and remains a significant landmark in the city center. Lilla Bommen – The Harbor & Iconic Sights Enjoy sailing into the North Sea as you reach Lilla Bommen, a key part of Gothenburg’s harbor. This area is home to the Göteborg Opera House, the Viking Barque Ship, and the distinctive Läppstiftet ("The Lipstick"), a red-and-white skyscraper offering panoramic city views. Water and snacks will be provided during the tour. Feskekörka – The Fish Church Cruising further along the Göta River, you will pass Feskekörka ("Fish Church"), a unique indoor fish market designed in Neo-Gothic style. Opened in 1874, this landmark, designed by architect Victor von Gegerfelt, is an essential stop for seafood lovers and architectural enthusiasts alike. Final Landmarks & Return As the tour continues, you will pass Stora Teatern, a historic theater known for its striking architecture, and Trädgårdsföreningen, a beautiful 19th-century garden park. At the end of the boat tour, we will drive you back to your hotel, concluding your memorable journey through Gothenburg’s waterways

First, you will visit the modern Oslo Opera House, which quickly became the city’s icon after its construction in 2008. Our guide will tell you about this building and the radical transformation of the neighborhood, which occurred during the last two decades. Next, you will stroll down Karl Johans gate, the city’s emblematic two-lane central street. That’s where you can truly appreciate Oslo's stunning 19th-century architecture. We will make the first stop on this street near Domkirke, or as the locals gently call this cathedral—the “Dom.” The city’s main church was built in the late 17th century and substantially reconstructed during the 19th century. Follow our guide’s lead and see the other prominent buildings on Oslo’s main street. Stortinget, the Parliament building, was erected during the second part of the 19th century when Norway was in a forced union with Sweden. You will also notice the Grand Hotel building nearby—renowned playwright Henrik Ibsen used to frequent its café. A statue dedicated to Ibsen stands in front of the neighboring National Theater, not far from another one that depicts Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson. The majestic Royal Palace of Oslo stands on a hill at the end of the street. Even though it was built for the very person this street is named after, Karl Johan has never got a chance to reside in this magnificent palace. Our tour guide will delve deeper into the story of the French general-turned-Swedish king and how he became the ruler of Norway. Before the tour concludes, you will visit one more iconic building—the red-brick Oslo City Hall. Day 1: Arrive in Reykjavík Make your way to Reykjavík, and check into your accommodation in the afternoon. Free day in Reykjavík.

Day 2: Explore the Golden Circle and South Coast The day starts with a pick-up from your accommodation in Reykjavík. First, we will head out to explore the famous Golden Circle, which includes Þingvellir National Park where Icelanders founded their parliament in the year 930 A.D., the oldest parliament in the world. The Circle includes Geysir hot springs and Gullfoss waterfall. Next, we will drive to the beautiful South Coast. Our first stop is at Seljalandsfoss, a unique opportunity to experience the power and wonder of nature. Don't view this one from a distance – the walking path will take you directly behind the waterfall itself. Next, we will stop at the scenic Skógafoss, where the water crashes down over sea cliffs that marked the coastline of Iceland long ago. Watch out for rainbows – the incredible spray from this waterfall makes it an ideal spot to catch one or even two at a time! The final stop of the day is at Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach, the home of the famous Reynisdrangar peaks, rumored to be the figures of two trolls caught in the sun and turned to stone, and a basalt column cave. After that, we will make our way to a country hotel near the charming village of Vík, where we will rest for the night.

Day 3: Trek and Hike on the Glacier The journey continues along the South coast in the direction of Skaftafell and Vatnajökull National Park. At Skaftafell, another of Iceland's three national parks, we will take a 3-hour glacier hike on one of Vatnajökull outlet glaciers, led by one of our skilled glacier guides. After that bracing experience, we will explore a little further Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon where we can expect to see floating icebergs and the occasional frolicking seal. Beside the glacier lake, we will find another black sand crystal beach, which is usually filled with clear icebergs that have floated back to shore. For the evening, we will lay our heads in accommodations in the pleasant seaside town of Höfn.

Day 4: Hike to East Fjords Waterfalls The scenery continues as we follow the coastline of the East Fjords to Egilsstaðir, a picturesque town on the banks of the Lagarfljót River. On the way there, we will go for a 3-hour hike to Hengifoss, one of the highest waterfalls in Iceland which drops into a striking gorge. Next is Litlanesfoss waterfall – look for the red strata climbing the walls around the waterfall, created by volcanic ash and basaltic lava over thousands of years as the cliff was formed in the heat of many mighty eruptions. We will then make our way to our accommodation for the night.

Day 5: Discover Lake Mývatn and Surroundings This day is filled with highlights of Iceland. Our first stop is at the magnificent Dettifoss, the largest waterfall in Iceland. Next, we head to the Lake Mývatn area. Here our first stop will be Námaskarð geothermal area, filled with mud pools and fumaroles, which are an interesting geological feature marking a vent for steam and hot gasses in the Earth's crust. We'll then make a stop at Mývatn Nature Baths, where you have the opportunity to bath in the hot spring pools. The entrance fee can be added when booking or paid on site. For those that don't wish to go in the water, they can stroll around the area and enjoy the views or sit down in the cafeteria. Next up, we will take a walk to the Hverfjall crater, caused by a volcano eruption 2500 years ago, and Dimmuborgir, the “dark cities” of lava formations that tower overhead. We will continue our drive around Lake Mývatn before heading in the direction of Akureyri, with a stop on the way at Goðafoss Waterfall. Our accommodation will be at an inviting country hotel near Akureyri, the second largest city in Iceland.

Day 6: Watch Whales and Explore the Tröllaskagi Peninsula We will start the day by exploring the town of Akureyri, the capital of North Iceland. Then, we will drive to the neighboring town of Dalvík where we go for a 3-hour whale watching tour in Eyjafjörður fjord. Take this opportunity to enjoy the wonders of sea life, including humpback whales, white-beaked dolphins, and the occasional blue whale! If fishing interests you, give sea angling a try and taste whatever you catch. Next we will travel the Tröllaskagi Peninsula, which will take us through a couple of fishing hamlets before we stop in the cozy village of Siglufjörður. Thereafter, we will head to West Iceland, where we will spend the night in a hotel in a small college community.

Day 7: Visit West Iceland Sights and Return to Reykjavík On this, our final day, we will find ourselves in West Iceland – an area which Lonely Planet voted as one of the best destinations in 2016. Borgarfjörður has many splendid sights and we will focus on these today. We stop at Deildartunguhver hot spring, the legendary waterfall, Barnafoss, (the Children's Waterfall), and the Hraunfossar cascade, the atmospheric very low and wide falls where the water emerges, literally straight out of the lava field. Next on the agenda is the historic and picturesque site of Reykholt, home to Snorri Sturluson, the Icelandic historian, lawyer, politician, poet and the author of some Icelandic Sagas. See Snorralaug, Snorri's pool, dabble your fingers and feel the temperature of the water in the place where Snorri is likely to have bathed! We will drive around scenic fjord, Hvalfjörður (Whale Fjord), on our way to back Reykjavík. We expect to arrive in the city around 5 – 6 pm.

GLOBAL SEED VAULT EVENING HIKE | DURATIOn 19:00-22:30 | ABOUT Ready to join us for an exciting evening hike to the summit of Blomsterdalen, next to the Svalbard Global Seed Vault? Learn more about this interesting and unique seed vault and experience the rich history of coal mining in this area of Svalbard. We will make our way to the top of Blomsterdalshøgda at 320 meters above sea level, where we will have a stunning view over the local area, Adventfjorden, Isfjorden, and maybe even the glaciers on the other side! We start our hike when our guide will pick you up from your accommodation. We drive up to the Svalbard Global Seed Vault to see it from the outside (as entrance is prohibited). Here we will learn more about this unique vault, which is located deep inside the mountain. After exploring this area we will start our hike at the foot of the mountain, slowly hiking our way up to the summit. On our way we will make sure to have enough short stops for us to enjoy the surroundings we are in, together with a warm drink and some sweets. Don’t forget to be on the lookout for possible wildlife, such as the Svalbard reindeer and the Arctic fox. Bergen to Bergen: Day Tour to Flåm incl. the Flåm Train & Nærøyfjord Cruise | Pick up / meeting point : Bergen Railway Station, Strømgaten 4, Bergen Overview Experience a day tour with breathtaking fjords, tall mountains and quaint villages. Visit Flåm and Voss on this eco-friendly journey, includeing the Bergen Railway, the Flåm Railway and the Nærøyfjord cruise with a fully electric ship. What's included? All tickets, each timed for the perfect day tour Your travel plan conveniently shared by e-mail E-tickets for Bergen railway: Bergen to Voss E-tickets for premium bus: Voss to Gudvangen E-tickets for fjord cruise: Gudvangen to Flåm E-tickets for Flåm railway: Flåm to Myrdal E-tickets for Bergen railway: Myrdal to Bergen What to expect? Explore Norway’s most breathtaking UNESCO-protected fjords and mountains on this unique round trip departing from Bergen. Journey through the countryside on the Bergen railway, cruise the deep Nærøyfjord alongside steep mountainsides, visit the village of Flåm and experience riding the scenic Flåm railway. Header photo: Torild Moland/Visit Norway. This full-day package takes you from Bergen to Voss, Gudvangen, the Nærøyfjord, Flåm, Myrdal and back to Bergen. Enjoy the freedom of a self-guided tour that allows you to explore Norway without following a guide. After booking you will receive a travel plan including all departure times and e-tickets for each leg of the journey, along with a detailed travel guide. This is a hassle-free day trip to the Norwegian fjords, with all tickets included: 1. Bergen to Voss: A Scenic Rail Adventure Our adventure begins from Bergen Railway Station around 8am. As you step aboard the Bergen Railway (Bergensbanen), prepare for a visual feast. The train winds through lush valleys, tunnels, and snow-capped peaks. Waterfalls cascade alongside the tracks, and charming villages peek out from the landscape. 2. Voss to Gudvangen: A Journey of Valleys and Cliffs From Voss, hop on a comfortable coach toward Gudvangen. The route takes you through valleys with lush forests against a backdrop of snow-covered mountaintops and winding fjords.Gudvangen awaits, a tiny village nestled between towering cliffs and the Nærøyfjord. Imagine Vikings once roaming these shores. Take a moment to breathe in the fjord’s majesty. 3. Gudvangen to Flåm: Cruising the Nærøyfjord Brace yourself for the highlight: the Nærøyfjord cruise. Step aboard an emission-free electric catamaran and sail through narrow passages. Steep cliffs rise on either side, waterfalls plunge into the fjord, and tranquility envelops you. Flåm beckons at the journey’s end. Explore Flåm, a charming village where the fjord meets the mountains. Visit the Flåm Railway Museum or take a short hike. 4. Flåm to Myrdal: The Original Flåm Railway Climb aboard the Flåm Railway (Flåmsbana), hailed as one of the world’s most beautiful train rides. It ascends steeply, revealing vistas of the Aurlandsfjord, passing by waterfalls and amazing views. Tunnels, bridges, and panoramic windows make this 20-kilometer journey unforgettable. Myrdal awaits at the mountaintop station. Breathe in the crisp air and marvel at this engineering feat that connects Flåm to the Bergen Railway. 5. Myrdal to Bergen: Descending to Coastal Beauty Rejoin the Bergen Railway for the descent. As you wind down from the mountains, the scenery transforms. Arrive back in Bergen around 8.45pm at night. Explore the iconic Bryggen district, savor fresh seafood at the fish market, and soak up maritime vibes.

Rovaniemi: Snowmobiling and Reindeer & Husky Sledding, Arctic Circle Highlights, with Free time in Santa Claus Village with Lunch | 9 AM | 7 Hrs Pick up / meeting point Arctic Circle Snowmobile Park office, Koskikatu 8, Rovaniemi Overview Explore the Arctic Circle Highlights by Snowmobile! Meet reindeer and huskies, explore the Santa Claus Village and ride snowmobiles through the forests of Arctic Circle. What's included? Pick-up/drop-off in central Rovaniemi Knowledgeable, English-speaking guide 1h snowmobiling on shared snowmobile (2 pers) Reindeer experience with 500m sleigh ride Alaskan Husky experience with 500m sleigh ride Approx. 2 hours free time in Santa Claus Village Winter clothes (overalls, boots and gloves) Other equipment (helmet and balaclava) Salmon soup lunch (vegetarian option available) What to expect? Experience an action-packed arctic journey where you get to ride snowmobiles through stunning wilderness, meet enchanting reindeer, and energetic Alaskan Huskies, enjoy traditional salmon soup lunch and explore the Santa Claus Village. Your day will start with transfer to the farm, where you will be able to ride your own reindeer sledge in a brief, 500m long ride. Your newly learned skills will be rewarded with a Reindeer Sledge Driver’s License! Next, make your way to the Alaskan Huskies where you will find these beautiful, loyal, and energetic companions. Experience the Alaskan Huskies in action on a 500m long sleigh ride. Enjoy a traditional salmon soup lunch during your visit and listen to the local reindeer herders as they tell you more about the herding lifestyle and how it is to be a reindeer herder in the 21st century. After the farm visit, your guide will provide snowmobile training before taking off on a 1-hour-long snowmobile adventure through Arctic Circle forests, and children under 150cm can try mini snowmobiling for 10 minutes on our mini-track. After the snowmobile journey, enjoy some free time to explore the Santa Claus Village. You have the opportunity to experience the Christmas atmosphere, step across the Arctic Circle, meet Santa Claus. Your day will conclude as your guide drops you off back to Rovaniemi.

Optiona at Add on Cost 117 EUR per person | Tromsø: Northern Lights Cruise with Silent Electric Ship | 19:00 | 4 Hrs Overview Embark on a journey into the profound darkness of the Arctic fjords and Polar nights. We leave Tromsø behind and navigate towards the area with the most promising weather conditions for the night. This could be northwards to Kvaløyvågen, southwards to Ramfjorden, or westwards along the southern part of Kvaløya island. What's included? Knowledgeable, English-speaking guide 3 hour cruise around Tromsø area Comfortable & warm indoor saloons Water and wifi complementary Light meal: soup and focaccia What to expect? The captain and crew collaborate, vigilantly searching for clear skies or a break in the cloud cover. As we anticipate the arrival of the northern lights, you can stay cozy and warm in our heated lounges. Enjoy a drink from our cafe and a snack while you wait. As the evening unfolds, our guides will impart their knowledge and personal experiences of the Northern Lights. They’ll share tales from around the globe, both mythical and scientific, about this celestial phenomenon. When fortune smiles upon us and the Northern Lights grace the sky, you can don your warm attire and step outside to marvel at the ethereal dance of Lady Aurora. Some nights, she illuminates the sky with her vibrant hues, while on others, she may be a tad reticent, barely visible or completely hidden. Our guides are on hand to assist you in capturing these magical moments in photographs. On the return journey, you’ll be treated to a spectacular view of the Arctic city of Tromsø, its skyline, and the renowned Arctic Cathedral, all beautifully framed by the water’s edge. Pick up / meeting point : Skarven Kro Restaurant, Kaigata 6, Tromsø

Tromsø: Reindeer Sledding, Reindeer Feeding & Sami Culture with meals | 10 AM | 5 Hrs Overview Glide through the unmatched beauty of the Norwegian winter wonderland on a traditional Sami sled, come meet our herd of 120 Reindeer and join our Sami guides in a cozy talk about their culture traditions and customs! What's included? Pick-up/drop-off in central Tromsø Scenic transfers (45 min each way) Knowledgeable, English-speaking guide Entrance to the fence and feeding the her Reindeer Sledding for 30 minutes approx. Hot drinks & hot meal (Sámi stew or veg option) Stories about the life and culture of the Sámi Pick up / meeting point : Radisson Blu Hotel, Sjøgata 7, Tromsø What to expect? Get to know our herd of 200 reindeer and join on a 30 minute sled ride while enjoying our beautiful, untouched Arctic nature and the Lyngen Alps on the horizon! You will be picked up outside Radisson Blu Hotel in Tromsø: just look for the guide wearing a blue Luhkka (traditional Sami poncho) and a bus with a big SLEDDING sign. Our guides will provide you with bracelets to indicate you will take part in the sled ride. After checking in with our guide, you will hop on a 45 minutes’ drive to our camp. On your way, you will be able to enjoy the beautiful Northern Norwegian mountains and upon arrival, you will be greeted by our Sami guide who will give a brief safety introduction and guide you to your activity! Part of the group will join the sled ride right away. On a circuit of 2.5km, immersed in Northern Norway breathtaking nature, you will try the oldest mean of transportation and feel like a real Sami in the Tundra! Then it will be time for the second group to take part in this lovely and ancient activity. After the sled tour, you will head towards the fence and feed our lovely reindeers (many of the reindeer will even eat from your hand!). Right after, it is time for lunch. We will gather in our Gamme (a modern interpretation of a traditional Sami hut) or in the Lavvu (a traditional Sami tent, much like a Tipi) where you will enjoy some hot drinks and taste Biddos, a traditional Sami stew served at celebrations, with Reindeer meat, carrots and potatoes. We also offer a vegan alternative, a veggie soup with lentils, carrots, broccoli and green beans. When we are all settled and comfortable, our Sami guide will tell you more about the Sami culture and history, they will show you some of our traditional handicrafts and clothes too. There will be also time for questions, feel free to participate and ask our guide. Curiosity is always welcome and encouraged! And lastly, there will be time for a bathroom break and for you to visit our lovely souvenir shop on site, before boarding the bus and going back to the city! Tromsø Lapland is established by authentic Saami people with long reindeer herding traditions and have the longest experience of running authentic Saami experience and culture tours in Tromsø, being established in 2009.

Knowledgeable, English-speaking guide 3 hour cruise around Tromsø area Comfortable & warm indoor saloons Water and wifi complementary Light meal: soup and focaccia What to expect? Our guides are on hand to assist you in capturing these magical moments in photographs. On the return journey, you’ll be treated to a spectacular view of the Arctic city of Tromsø, its skyline, and the renowned Arctic Cathedral, all beautifully framed by the water’s edge. Tromsø Dog Sledding at at Breivikeidet with Lunch | 08:30 or 11:30 Meeting Point : Tromsø (Prostneset): 08:30 > Check-in at Prostneset Bus Terminal About the tour. Our dog sledding is located only a 45-minute drive from Tromsø, at the gateway to the Lyngen Alps. This area gives you stunning views over the majestic mountain peaks (up to 1400 meters!) and the fjord at the same time! Our tour involves 60 minutes of dogsledding in a thrilling ride along tree-lined trails and through open terrain. A briefing on how to handle the sled will be given before the trip. Reykjavik: 3-Day Winter Minibus Group Tour | South Coast, Ice Cave & Golden Circle - Meeting point: Hotel pick-up - Time: 08:00 am - Join us for a three-day adventure with 2 nights accommodation, ice cave tour, glacier hike and high chances of Northern Lights. Experience the amazing Blue Ice Cave, the powerful waterfalls, hike on top of a glacier and admire the Glacier Lagoon and Diamond Beach. Includes: Pick-up/drop off in central Reykjavik, Professional, English-speaking guide, Hotel stays with breakfast and private bathroom, Travel in premum vehicle with WiFi on board, Small-group, local Iceland experience, Day 1: Visit to Thingvellir National Park, Day 1: Visit to the Geysir geothermal area, Day 1: Visit to Gullfoss waterfall, Day 2: Visit to Seljalandsfoss waterfall, Day 2: Visit to Skogafoss waterfall, Day 2: Visit to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach, Day 3: Jökulsárlón Amphibian boat ride, Day 3: Visit to Diamond Beach & Ice Cave, Day 3 Glacier hike with gear and certified guide, All taxes and fees included

Day 1: The Golden Circle and Northern Lights - Start at 8 am in Reykjavík and head to the famous Golden Circle area. Explore the historic and scenic Thingvellir National Park. Experience the power of Gullfoss waterfall and capture stunning photos. Visit the Geysir geothermal area, see Strokkur geyser erupting, and experience the hot springs. Spend your night in a countryside hotel or guesthouse with private bathroom and breakfast included. Hotels offered vary based on availability, and are typically cozy and local 3-star hotels and guesthouses along the route.

Day 2: The South Coast incl. Seljalandsfoss, Skogafoss and Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach - The first stop is at Seljalandsfoss waterfall where you can walk behind the tumbling water flow and feel the vibrations of the water hitting the ground. Thirsty? Just open your mouth. Right next to it is the waterfall Gljúfrabúi which snugly tucked in a gorge hidden from most. Gljúfrabúi actually means Canyon Dweller in English. To reach the waterfall, you must first test your balance by bouncing on rocks lying in the river bed. A failure means instant foot wetness and a good laugh by your co-travellers. Next, meet the pearl of the South Coast, Skógafoss waterfall. Majestically tucked in a wide gorge, the waterfall tumbles down 60 metres from up above a cliff into a small river, producing a cloud of mist and spray that rainbows like to dance in during sunshine. Try to warm up for the glacier by running up the 527 steps to the top... Your guide will be timing you! Heading further east, we visit the black sand beach of Reynisfjara where the Atlantic coastline presents massive waves hitting the unique basalt columns in the cliffs above the sand. Rock pillars in the water and the cliffs of Dýrhólaey are seen in the distance. Glacier Hike complete our perfect adventure we will hike an outlet glacier spawning from the one of the largest glaciers in the country. After meeting our highly trained glacier guides and strapping on our safety and glacier equipment, including helmets, harnesses, crampons and ice axes we hike on the ice for an hour and a half. A spectacular experience and opportunity to learn more about this breathtaking and increasingly rare natural phenomena. Spend your night in a countryside hotel or guesthouse with private bathroom and breakfast included. Hotels offered vary based on availability, and are typically cozy and local 3-star hotels and guesthouses along the route.

Day 3: The South Coast incl. Jökulsarlon Glacier Lagoon, Diamond Beach and Glacier Hiking and Ice Caving - Jökulsárlón, the Glacier Lagoon, is a 200m deep glacial lake fed by Breiðamerkurjökull, an outlet glacier of Europe’s largest glacier. Fed by enormous icebergs all year round, the lagoon is usually filled with ice that floats south. We give you the opportunity to book a boat ride between the icebergs during summer time and get a closer look of the millenary ice. If boating is not your thing, then we walk alongside the glacier lagoon enjoying the magnificent views and dead silence of Icelandic nature. Diamond Beach: on the other side of the road the icebergs from Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon float into the Atlantic Ocean where they are quickly thrown back to shore by the tide and winds. This black sand beach is full of smaller ice rocks in all shapes and sizes, sparkling like diamonds in the daylight. The ice itself comes in all shades of white and blue forming beautiful contrasts, guaranteed to make your Instagram account pop! This guided walk leads you through the narrow lanes and ancient passages where executioners once lived and where dramatic tales shaped the city’s past. As you wander through the German quarter and slip into the narrow passage of Marten Trotzig, the rich world of medieval Stockholm slowly comes to life. Your journey continues through places where history still sleeps untouched, including a visit to the Rose Gate, the oldest surviving gate in the city. Here you will see remnants from long ago that still hold the stories of those who walked these paths. This walk offers a richer understanding of Old Town, blending atmosphere and storytelling for a memorable and meaningful experience.

Reykjavík: 8 Day - Ultimate Iceland Ring Road & Volcano Hike Overview Discover Iceland's wonders: waterfalls, geysers, ice caves, and the Icelandic Highlands What's included? Pick-up/drop-off in central Reykjavik Professional, English-speaking guide Optional activities: Katla Ice Cave Optional activities: Vök Baths Optional activities: Whale Watching 7-night hotel accommodation Breakfast and private bathroom Free Wi-Fi on the bus exclusions : Food and drinks not included (except hotel breakfast)

Day 1: Embark on an unforgettable journey through Iceland's breathtaking landscapes on the Ultimate Icelandic Adventure Tour. Your adventure begins with a pick-up in Reykjavík, followed by a scenic drive to Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Immerse yourself in the historic and geological wonders of Þingvellir, where you can explore the dramatic rift valley and learn about Iceland's fascinating history. Continuing the journey, you'll drive to the Geysir geothermal area, where powerful geysers erupt and create a mesmerizing spectacle. Experience the thrill of watching Strokkur geyser shoot hot water high into the air. Next, head to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, one of Iceland's most iconic natural wonders. Marvel at the sheer power and beauty of the cascading falls before enjoying a lunch stop at the site. After lunch, your adventure takes you to the enchanting Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can take a walk behind the cascading water curtain for a unique perspective. Continue to the awe-inspiring Skógafoss waterfall, known for its impressive height and thundering water. Capture stunning photos and feel the mist on your face as you stand in awe of these majestic falls. Next, visit the black sand beach of Reynisfjara, famous for its striking basalt columns and towering sea stacks. Explore the otherworldly landscape and learn about the fascinating folklore surrounding this area. Finally, you'll drive to your hotel on the South Coast, where you can relax and recharge for the next day's adventures.

Day 2: After a delicious breakfast at the hotel, you'll embark on another day of exploration. Begin with a visit to the charming coastal village of Vík, known for its picturesque black sand beaches and dramatic rock formations. Take in the breathtaking views of the Reynisdrangar sea stacks and Reynisfjara Beach before continuing your journey. The highlight of the day is the Katla Ice Cave, a magical natural wonder hidden beneath the Mýrdalsjökull glacier. Explore the ice cave and marvel at the stunning blue hues and intricate ice formations. Alternatively, you can choose to spend some free time exploring the area and taking in the serene beauty of the surrounding landscapes. After the ice cave adventure, enjoy a delicious lunch in Vík before driving to the stunning Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon. Walk along the canyon rim and be captivated by the sheer scale and beauty of this geological marvel. Continuing eastward, you'll arrive at Jökulsárlón, a glacial lagoon filled with massive icebergs. Take a boat tour or simply enjoy the mesmerizing sight of icebergs floating in crystal-clear waters. Don't miss the nearby Diamond Beach, where ice chunks from the lagoon wash up on the black sand, creating a magical contrast. In the late afternoon, drive to your hotel in Höfn, where you can relax and reflect on the day's adventures.

Day 3: Start your day with a hearty breakfast at the hotel before continuing your Icelandic adventure. Today's journey takes you to the remote and beautiful eastern part of Iceland. Drive to Djúpivogur, a charming fishing village known for its picturesque harbor and stunning mountain views. Take a moment to explore the village and appreciate the tranquility of this coastal gem. Continue your drive to Egilsstaðir, where you can enjoy a delicious lunch and take a break before the next leg of the journey. Afterward, venture to Borgarfjörður Eystri, a hidden gem famous for its puffin colonies and rugged beauty. Watch these adorable seabirds in their natural habitat and explore the quaint village. Next, drive to Vök Baths, a geothermal oasis nestled on the shores of Lake Urriðavatn. Immerse yourself in the soothing warm waters and take in the panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and landscapes. Relax and rejuvenate in these natural hot springs before heading to your hotel at Egilsstaðir, where you can unwind and prepare for the next day's adventures.

Day 4: After enjoying a delicious breakfast, it's time to hit the road again. Begin your day with a visit to Stuðlagil Canyon, known for its striking basalt columns and stunning blue glacial river. Explore this hidden gem and witness the unique formations that make it a photographer's paradise. Continuing your journey, you'll arrive at Dettifoss, Europe's most powerful waterfall. Feel the raw power and hear the thundering sound as water plummets into the canyon below. Take your time to appreciate the sheer scale and grandeur of this natural wonder. Next, visit the Námaskarð geothermal area, known for its otherworldly landscapes and bubbling mud pots. Take a walk among the steaming vents and colorful mineral deposits, getting a glimpse of Iceland's geothermal activity up close. Your adventure continues with a visit to Dimmuborgir, a mystical lava field with eerie rock formations and lava pillars. Explore the area and discover the folklore and legends associated with these dark and dramatic landscapes. Next, visit Skútustaðagígar, a collection of pseudocraters formed by volcanic activity. Take a walk along the rim of these unique formations and enjoy the panoramic views of the surrounding area. Make a stop at Goðafoss, the "Waterfall of the Gods," known for its beauty and historical significance. Learn about the ancient Icelandic sagas that surround this majestic waterfall and take in the breathtaking views. After a day filled with natural wonders, check into Hótel Akureyri, where you can relax and reflect on the day's experiences.

Day 5: Start your day with a delicious breakfast before exploring the charming town of Akureyri, known as the "Capital of the North." Take a leisurely walk to the harbor and embark on a thrilling Whale Watching Tour. Keep your eyes peeled for magnificent whales as they breach the surface of the ocean, creating unforgettable memories. After the whale-watching adventure, enjoy a leisurely lunch in Akureyri before continuing your journey. Drive to Glaumbær, a historic turf farm and open-air museum that offers a glimpse into Iceland's rural past. Step back in time as you explore the traditional turf houses and gain insight into the country's rich cultural heritage. Next, visit Borgarvirki, an ancient volcanic plug that served as a fortress in Iceland's Viking Age. Learn about its historical significance and enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes. Continue your journey to Hvítserkur, a striking rock formation rising from the sea. Marvel at the unique shape of this monolith and let your imagination run wild as you contemplate the mythical tales associated with it. Make your way to Kolugljúfur, a beautiful canyon named after the giantess Kola who, according to folklore, used to live there. Admire the cascading waterfalls and the serene beauty of the area. Finally, drive to the hotel in Laugarbakki, where you can relax, enjoy the peaceful surroundings, and reflect on the day's adventures.

Day 6: On the final day of your Icelandic adventure, savor a delicious breakfast before continuing your journey. Drive to Grábrók, a volcanic crater known for its stunning views and unique geological features. Take a short walk to the rim and soak in the panoramic vistas. Next, visit Glanni waterfall, a serene and picturesque cascade nestled in the beautiful Húsafell area. Enjoy the peaceful ambiance and let the sounds of nature soothe your soul. Continue your exploration to Hraunfossar, a series of cascading waterfalls flowing through lava fields, creating a mesmerizing sight. Marvel at the contrast between the vibrant blue water and the dark volcanic rocks. Afterward, visit Sturlureykir, a traditional Icelandic horse farm. Experience the unique charm of Icelandic horses and learn about their history and significance to the country's culture. Make a stop at Deildartunguhver, Europe's most powerful hot spring. Witness the boiling water gushing from the ground and feel the heat emanating from this geothermal wonder. Next, drive to Reykjavík, where you´ll check into your hotel and have a free afternoon.

Day 7: After breakfast and checking out, you'll be picked up from your hotel and driven towards the Snæfellsnes Peninsula in West Iceland. You'll explore the mesmerizing beauty of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and the iconic Kirkjufell Mountain, which has earned the nickname "Arrowhead Mountain" for its distinctive shape. Discover the dramatic landscapes, lava fields, and coastal cliffs. Your stops for the day will also include Djúplalónssandur pebble stone beach, Arnarstapi village, Búðir Black Church, and Seal Beach at Ytri-Tunga. After the sightseeing is done at the peninsula, you'll head back to Reykjavík, where you'll check into your hotel and rest for your final day of the tour.

Day 8: On this day, you'll embark on an unforgettable adventure Volcano Hike to Iceland’s newest eruption site at Fagradalsfjall. This guided tour takes you from Reykjavík to the heart of the Reykjanes peninsula, where you’ll hike through surreal lava fields and witness the raw power of nature up close. Whether the volcano is active or quietly simmering, the dramatic landscape and glowing terrain offer a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Perfect for thrill-seekers and nature lovers alike, this journey delivers stunning views, expert guidance, and a true taste of Iceland’s volcanic soul. After your time on the peninsula, you will head back towards Reykjavík. Once we reach Reykjavík, we'll drop you off at your preferred location, and that will mark the end of your journey around Iceland.

Group Tour Starts: 8-Day Holiday Package Ring Road & Landmannalaugar | Overview Discover Iceland from Reykjavík across the Golden Circle, South Coast, Glacier Lagoon region, East Fjords, North Iceland, West Iceland, and the Snæfellsnes Peninsula, including the Highlands at Landmannalaugar. Pick-up/drop-off in central Reykjavik Knowledgeable, English-speaking guide 7 nights hotel accommodation incl. breakfast National park entry and parking fees Free Wi-Fi available on board the bus Day 1: The Golden Circle and South Coast Day 2: The South Coast and Jökulsárlón Day 3: Eastern Iceland and Egilsstaðir Day 4: North-East Iceland and Akureyri Day 5: North Iceland and Laugarbakki Day 6: West Iceland and Borgarnes Day 7: Snæfellsnes Peninsula and Reykjavík Day 8: Landmannalaugar and the Highlands What to expect? Over 8 days and 7 nights, explore Iceland’s most stunning landscapes, from Reykjavík to the Golden Circle, South Coast, East Fjords, North Iceland, West Iceland, and the Snæfellsnes Peninsula, including the Highlands at Landmannalaugar. Your journey begins with geysers, waterfalls, and black sand beaches, continues along dramatic coastlines, glaciers, ice caves, canyons, and lava fields, and concludes with whale watching, geothermal baths, volcanic craters, and the striking scenery of Snæfellsnes. Stay in comfortable hotels with breakfast included, and travel in a well-equipped minibus with an experienced guide. Transportation between destinations, guided activities, and accommodation are all included. Simply arrive in Reykjavík on your selected date and follow the itinerary. Book your return flight from Reykjavík after the tour ends on Day 8. This guided holiday is suitable for anyone in normal health and ready for light outdoor activities.

Day 1: Explore the Golden Circle and South Coast Embark on an unforgettable journey through Iceland's breathtaking landscapes on the Ultimate Icelandic Adventure Tour. Your adventure begins with a pick-up in Reykjavík, followed by a scenic drive to Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Immerse yourself in the historic and geological wonders of Þingvellir, where you can explore the dramatic rift valley and learn about Iceland's fascinating history. Continuing the journey, you'll drive to the Geysir geothermal area, where powerful geysers erupt and create a mesmerizing spectacle. Experience the thrill of watching Strokkur geyser shoot hot water high into the air. Next, head to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, one of Iceland's most iconic natural wonders. Marvel at the sheer power and beauty of the cascading falls before enjoying a lunch stop at the site. After lunch, your adventure takes you to the enchanting Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can take a walk behind the cascading water curtain for a unique perspective. Continue to the awe-inspiring Skógafoss waterfall, known for its impressive height and thundering water. Capture stunning photos and feel the mist on your face as you stand in awe of these majestic falls. Next, visit the black sand beach of Reynisfjara, famous for its striking basalt columns and towering sea stacks. Explore the otherworldly landscape and learn about the fascinating folklore surrounding this area. Finally, you'll drive to your hotel on the South Coast, where you can relax and recharge for the next day's adventures.

Day 2: Discover Ice Caves and Glacier Lagoons After a delicious breakfast at the hotel, you'll embark on another day of exploration. Begin with a visit to the charming coastal village of Vík, known for its picturesque black sand beaches and dramatic rock formations. Take in the breathtaking views of the Reynisdrangar sea stacks and Reynisfjara Beach before continuing your journey. The highlight of the day is the Katla Ice Cave, a magical natural wonder hidden beneath the Mýrdalsjökull glacier. Explore the ice cave and marvel at the stunning blue hues and intricate ice formations. Alternatively, you can choose to spend some free time exploring the area and taking in the serene beauty of the surrounding landscapes. After the ice cave adventure, enjoy a delicious lunch in Vík before driving to the stunning Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon. Walk along the canyon rim and be captivated by the sheer scale and beauty of this geological marvel. Continuing eastward, you'll arrive at Jökulsárlón, a glacial lagoon filled with massive icebergs. Take a boat tour or simply enjoy the mesmerizing sight of icebergs floating in crystal-clear waters. Don't miss the nearby Diamond Beach, where ice chunks from the lagoon wash up on the black sand, creating a magical contrast. In the late afternoon, drive to your hotel in Höfn, where you can relax and reflect on the day's adventures

Day 3: Journey Through the East Fjords and Soak in Geothermal Baths Start your day with a hearty breakfast at the hotel before continuing your Icelandic adventure. Today's journey takes you to the remote and beautiful eastern part of Iceland. Drive to Djúpivogur, a charming fishing village known for its picturesque harbor and stunning mountain views. Take a moment to explore the village and appreciate the tranquility of this coastal gem. Continue your drive to Egilsstaðir, where you can enjoy a delicious lunch and take a break before the next leg of the journey. Afterward, venture to Borgarfjörður Eystri, a hidden gem famous for its puffin colonies and rugged beauty. Watch these adorable seabirds in their natural habitat and explore the quaint village. Next, drive to Vök Baths, a geothermal oasis nestled on the shores of Lake Urriðavatn. Immerse yourself in the soothing warm waters and take in the panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and landscapes. Relax and rejuvenate in these natural hot springs before heading to your hotel at Egilsstaðir, where you can unwind and prepare for the next day's adventures.

Day 4: Traverse North Iceland’s Waterfalls and Volcanic Landscapes After enjoying a delicious breakfast, it's time to hit the road again. Begin your day with a visit to Stuðlagil Canyon, known for its striking basalt columns and stunning blue glacial river. Explore this hidden gem and witness the unique formations that make it a photographer's paradise. Continuing your journey, you'll arrive at Dettifoss, Europe's most powerful waterfall. Feel the raw power and hear the thundering sound as water plummets into the canyon below. Take your time to appreciate the sheer scale and grandeur of this natural wonder. Next, visit the Námaskarð geothermal area, known for its otherworldly landscapes and bubbling mud pots. Take a walk among the steaming vents and colorful mineral deposits, getting a glimpse of Iceland's geothermal activity up close. Your adventure continues with a visit to Dimmuborgir, a mystical lava field with eerie rock formations and lava pillars. Explore the area and discover the folklore and legends associated with these dark and dramatic landscapes. Next, visit Skútustaðagígar, a collection of pseudocraters formed by volcanic activity. Take a walk along the rim of these unique formations and enjoy the panoramic views of the surrounding area. Make a stop at Goðafoss, the "Waterfall of the Gods," known for its beauty and historical significance. Learn about the ancient Icelandic sagas that surround this majestic waterfall and take in the breathtaking views. After a day filled with natural wonders, check into Hótel Akureyri, where you can relax and reflect on the day's experiences.

Day 5: Experience Whale Watching and Coastal Heritage Start your day with a delicious breakfast before exploring the charming town of Akureyri, known as the "Capital of the North." Take a leisurely walk to the harbor and embark on a thrilling Whale Watching Tour. Keep your eyes peeled for magnificent whales as they breach the surface of the ocean, creating unforgettable memories. After the whale-watching adventure, enjoy a leisurely lunch in Akureyri before continuing your journey. Drive to Glaumbær, a historic turf farm and open-air museum that offers a glimpse into Iceland's rural past. Step back in time as you explore the traditional turf houses and gain insight into the country's rich cultural heritage. Next, visit Borgarvirki, an ancient volcanic plug that served as a fortress in Iceland's Viking Age. Learn about its historical significance and enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes. Continue your journey to Hvítserkur, a striking rock formation rising from the sea. Marvel at the unique shape of this monolith and let your imagination run wild as you contemplate the mythical tales associated with it. Make your way to Kolugljúfur, a beautiful canyon named after the giantess Kola who, according to folklore, used to live there. Admire the cascading waterfalls and the serene beauty of the area. Finally, drive to the hotel in Laugarbakki, where you can relax, enjoy the peaceful surroundings, and reflect on the day's adventures.

Day 6: Climb Craters and Explore West Iceland’s Hot Springs On the final day of your Icelandic adventure, savor a delicious breakfast before continuing your journey. Drive to Grábrók, a volcanic crater known for its stunning views and unique geological features. Take a short walk to the rim and soak in the panoramic vistas. Next, visit Glanni waterfall, a serene and picturesque cascade nestled in the beautiful Húsafell area. Enjoy the peaceful ambiance and let the sounds of nature soothe your soul. Continue your exploration to Hraunfossar, a series of cascading waterfalls flowing through lava fields, creating a mesmerizing sight. Marvel at the contrast between the vibrant blue water and the dark volcanic rocks. Afterward, visit Sturlureykir, a traditional Icelandic horse farm. Experience the unique charm of Icelandic horses and learn about their history and significance to the country's culture. Make a stop at Deildartunguhver, Europe's most powerful hot spring. Witness the boiling water gushing from the ground and feel the heat emanating from this geothermal wonder. Next, drive to Borgarnes, where you´ll check in to your hotel and have a free afternoon.

Day 7: Explore the Snæfellsnes Peninsula After breakfast and checking out, you'll be picked up from your hotel and drive towards the Snæfellsnes Peninsula in West Iceland. You'll explore the mesmerizing beauty of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and the iconic Kirkjufell Mountain, which has earned the nickname "Arrowhead Mountain" for its distinctive shape. Discover the dramatic landscapes, lava fields, and coastal cliffs. Your stops for the day will also include Djúplalónssandur pebble stone beach, Arnarstapi village, Búðir Black Church, and Seal Beach at Ytri-Tunga. After the sightseeing is done at the peninsula, you'll head back to Reykjavík, where you'll check into your hotel and rest for your final day of the tour.

Day 8: Venture into the Highlands at Landmannalaugar On this day, you'll embark on an unforgettable journey to Landmannalaugar, Iceland's captivating highland region. This day offers a unique opportunity to explore one of the country's most remote and stunning areas. Landmannalaugar is famous for its colorful rhyolite mountains, natural hot springs, and breathtaking hiking trails. As you venture deep into the heart of Iceland's wilderness, you'll encounter rugged terrain and ever-changing landscapes. At Landmannalaugar you have the chance of bathing in the hot pools in the area and do some hiking up to Mt. Brennisteinsalda. After your time in Landmannalaugar, you will head back towards Reykjavík. However, on the way back, we will make a couple of sightseeing stops, including at one of Icelands´s highest waterfalls, Háifoss. Once we reach Reykjavík, we'll drop you off at your preferred location and that will mark the end of your journey around Iceland.

Day 1: Arrive in Reykjavík Make your way to Reykjavík, and check into your accommodation in the afternoon. Free day in Reykjavík.

Day 2: Explore the Golden Circle and South Coast The day starts with a pick-up from your accommodation in Reykjavík. First, we will head out to explore the famous Golden Circle, which includes Þingvellir National Park where Icelanders founded their parliament in the year 930 A.D., the oldest parliament in the world. The Circle includes Geysir hot springs and Gullfoss waterfall. Next, we will drive to the beautiful South Coast. Our first stop is at Seljalandsfoss, a unique opportunity to experience the power and wonder of nature. Don't view this one from a distance – the walking path will take you directly behind the waterfall itself. Next, we will stop at the scenic Skógafoss, where the water crashes down over sea cliffs that marked the coastline of Iceland long ago. Watch out for rainbows – the incredible spray from this waterfall makes it an ideal spot to catch one or even two at a time! The final stop of the day is at Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach, the home of the famous Reynisdrangar peaks, rumored to be the figures of two trolls caught in the sun and turned to stone, and a basalt column cave. After that, we will make our way to a country hotel near the charming village of Vík, where we will rest for the night

Day 3: Trek and Hike on the Glacier The journey continues along the South coast in the direction of Skaftafell and Vatnajökull National Park. At Skaftafell, another of Iceland's three national parks, we will take a 3-hour glacier hike on one of Vatnajökull outlet glaciers, led by one of our skilled glacier guides. After that bracing experience, we will explore a little further Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon where we can expect to see floating icebergs and the occasional frolicking seal. Beside the glacier lake, we will find another black sand crystal beach, which is usually filled with clear icebergs that have floated back to shore. For the evening, we will lay our heads in accommodations in the pleasant seaside town of Höfn.

Day 4: Hike to East Fjords Waterfalls The scenery continues as we follow the coastline of the East Fjords to Egilsstaðir, a picturesque town on the banks of the Lagarfljót River. On the way there, we will go for a 3-hour hike to Hengifoss, one of the highest waterfalls in Iceland which drops into a striking gorge. Next is Litlanesfoss waterfall – look for the red strata climbing the walls around the waterfall, created by volcanic ash and basaltic lava over thousands of years as the cliff was formed in the heat of many mighty eruptions. We will then make our way to our accommodation for the night.

Day 5: Discover Lake Mývatn and Surroundings This day is filled with highlights of Iceland. Our first stop is at the magnificent Dettifoss, the largest waterfall in Iceland. Next, we head to the Lake Mývatn area. Here our first stop will be Námaskarð geothermal area, filled with mud pools and fumaroles, which are an interesting geological feature marking a vent for steam and hot gasses in the Earth's crust. We'll then make a stop at Mývatn Nature Baths, where you have the opportunity to bath in the hot spring pools. The entrance fee can be added when booking or paid on site. For those that don't wish to go in the water, they can stroll around the area and enjoy the views or sit down in the cafeteria. Next up, we will take a walk to the Hverfjall crater, caused by a volcano eruption 2500 years ago, and Dimmuborgir, the “dark cities” of lava formations that tower overhead. We will continue our drive around Lake Mývatn before heading in the direction of Akureyri, with a stop on the way at Goðafoss Waterfall. Our accommodation will be at an inviting country hotel near Akureyri, the second largest city in Iceland.

Day 6: Watch Whales and Explore the Tröllaskagi Peninsula We will start the day by exploring the town of Akureyri, the capital of North Iceland. Then, we will drive to the neighboring town of Dalvík where we go for a 3-hour whale watching tour in Eyjafjörður fjord. Take this opportunity to enjoy the wonders of sea life, including humpback whales, white-beaked dolphins, and the occasional blue whale! If fishing interests you, give sea angling a try and taste whatever you catch. Next we will travel the Tröllaskagi Peninsula, which will take us through a couple of fishing hamlets before we stop in the cozy village of Siglufjörður. Thereafter, we will head to West Iceland, where we will spend the night in a hotel in a small college community.

Day 7: Visit West Iceland Sights and Return to Reykjavík On this, our final day, we will find ourselves in West Iceland – an area which Lonely Planet voted as one of the best destinations in 2016. Borgarfjörður has many splendid sights and we will focus on these today. We stop at Deildartunguhver hot spring, the legendary waterfall, Barnafoss, (the Children's Waterfall), and the Hraunfossar cascade, the atmospheric very low and wide falls where the water emerges, literally straight out of the lava field. Next on the agenda is the historic and picturesque site of Reykholt, home to Snorri Sturluson, the Icelandic historian, lawyer, politician, poet and the author of some Icelandic Sagas. See Snorralaug, Snorri's pool, dabble your fingers and feel the temperature of the water in the place where Snorri is likely to have bathed! We will drive around scenic fjord, Hvalfjörður (Whale Fjord), on our way to back Reykjavík. We expect to arrive in the city around 5 – 6 pm.

Oslo : Essential Oslo, City Center Guided Walking Tour | 10 AM | 2 Hrs | Experience the beauty of the Norwegian capital on foot with this walking tour See all the major sights and attractions in a pedestrian part of Oslo Save money with this great value pass Meet our guide near the University of Oslo, Start your day with a guided walking tour of Oslo's most popular sights and landmarks. *From 17 November to 30 December, the Christmas Walk will replace the Essential Oslo Tour. Explore the major attractions of the vibrant Norwegian capital on our bestselling city tour. Meet our guide near the University of Oslo, in the city’s heart, and embark on a thrilling urban adventure! First, you will visit the modern Oslo Opera House, which quickly became the city’s icon after its construction in 2008. Our guide will tell you about this building and the radical transformation of the neighborhood, which occurred during the last two decades. Next, you will stroll down Karl Johans gate, the city’s emblematic two-lane central street. That’s where you can truly appreciate Oslo's stunning 19th-century architecture. We will make the first stop on this street near Domkirke, or as the locals gently call this cathedral—the “Dom.” The city’s main church was built in the late 17th century and substantially reconstructed during the 19th century. Follow our guide’s lead and see the other prominent buildings on Oslo’s main street. Stortinget, the Parliament building, was erected during the second part of the 19th century when Norway was in a forced union with Sweden. You will also notice the Grand Hotel building nearby—renowned playwright Henrik Ibsen used to frequent its café. A statue dedicated to Ibsen stands in front of the neighboring National Theater, not far from another one that depicts Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson. The majestic Royal Palace of Oslo stands on a hill at the end of the street. Even though it was built for the very person this street is named after, Karl Johan has never got a chance to reside in this magnificent palace. Our tour guide will delve deeper into the story of the French general-turned-Swedish king and how he became the ruler of Norway. Before the tour concludes, you will visit one more iconic building—the red-brick Oslo City Hall. Its construction took decades to finish, but today, this place embodies the spirit of Oslo (and Norway in general)—the walls of this building are painted with numerous frescoes depicting the history of this Scandinavian country. Join our walking tour today to explore Oslo in a fun and exciting way!

Meet our guide near the University of Oslo, in the city’s heart, and embark on a thrilling urban adventure! First, you will visit the modern Oslo Opera House, which quickly became the city’s icon after its construction in 2008. Our guide will tell you about this building and the radical transformation of the neighborhood, which occurred during the last two decades. Next, you will stroll down Karl Johans gate, the city’s emblematic two-lane central street. That’s where you can truly appreciate Oslo's stunning 19th-century architecture. We will make the first stop on this street near Domkirke, or as the locals gently call this cathedral—the “Dom.” The city’s main church was built in the late 17th century and substantially reconstructed during the 19th century. Follow our guide’s lead and see the other prominent buildings on Oslo’s main street. Stortinget, the Parliament building, was erected during the second part of the 19th century when Norway was in a forced union with Sweden. You will also notice the Grand Hotel building nearby—renowned playwright Henrik Ibsen used to frequent its café. A statue dedicated to Ibsen stands in front of the neighboring National Theater, not far from another one that depicts Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson. The majestic Royal Palace of Oslo stands on a hill at the end of the street. Even though it was built for the very person this street is named after, Karl Johan has never got a chance to reside in this magnificent palace. Our tour guide will delve deeper into the story of the French general-turned-Swedish king and how he became the ruler of Norway. Before the tour concludes, you will visit one more iconic building—the red-brick Oslo City Hall. Its construction took decades to finish, but today, this place embodies the spirit of Oslo (and Norway in general)—the walls of this building are painted with numerous frescoes depicting the history of this Scandinavian country. Join our walking tour today to explore Oslo in a fun and exciting way!
